children: US crude oil inventories fell by 300,000 barrels in the week ended September 4th, following a 2.6 million-barrel decline in the previous week.
Commercial crude inventories excluding the SPR have fallen by just over 48 million barrels over the past 21 weeks, while US crude inventories are up 2.8 million barrels year to date.
Another 1.2 million barrels were released from the SPR to support commercial inventories, bringing total SPR holdings to 285.4 million barrels.
The generally accepted operational minimum is 250-300 million barrels.
Cushing inventories fell by 300,000 barrels after rising by 200,000 barrels the previous week.
US production rose to 13.862 million bpd in the week ended August 28th, from 13.843 million bpd.
Gasoline inventories fell by 1.9 million barrels, while distillate inventories rose by 2 million barrels.

title: US Crude Inventories Fall in Early September
